content:
Two numbers — 22/7 and 3.14 — and two formulas carry this whole chapter. What the IMO adds is judgement. A wheel question wants circumference; a ring question wants area. Choosing fast is the skill. Scroll down for the free IMO Class 7 Circles online test. Ten Olympiad-pattern MCQs, instant scoring. Under every question sits an explanation you can learn from.

What the IMO asks from Circles in Class 7

  • Radius, diameter, chord and arc vocabulary.
  • Circumference problems: wheels and rotations.
  • Area of circles, semicircles and rings.
  • Combined figures: circle in a square.
  • Choosing 22/7 vs 3.14 wisely.

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • Diameter = 2 × radius: a 14 cm radius means a 28 cm diameter.
  • A wheel covers exactly one circumference per rotation.
  • Ring area = π(R² − r²) — subtract areas, not radii.
  • Perimeter of a semicircle = πr + 2r (students forget the diameter).

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Using radius where the question gives diameter.
  • Leaving out the straight edge in a semicircle perimeter.
  • Subtracting radii instead of areas for a ring.
